speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment of your gait and limb ataxia, when did you first notice these symptoms, and have they been progressing steadily or fluctuating over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. To help narrow down the cause, have you experienced any other neurological symptoms such as difficulty speaking, swallowing, or double vision?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, I am concerned about the possibility of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). Have you experienced any changes in your memory, personality, or vision, or have you had any recent headaches or fevers?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of gait and limb ataxia with right-sided weakness in a patient on natalizumab is highly suggestive of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). To confirm this suspicion, I need to visualize the brain for characteristic demyelinating lesions.
REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain
